# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✌ 👌 ✌ ☝ 👌 ☝ 🤟]

I see the bomb’s current state: display `0`, white light, and three wires in order yellow, green, blue. Mute’s gesture sequence has no established meaning yet, so I will relay it literally to Blind and ask Mute to provide the manual’s instruction through a defined gesture code.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, white light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Please send the manual instruction in gestures; I will relay it to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb view: display 0, white light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signalled this gesture sequence: 🤟 ✌ 👌 ✌ ☝ 👌 ☝ 🤟. Its meaning is not established yet.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👌 🤟 👌 ☝]

The bomb’s light has changed from white to purple; the display and wire colors remain unchanged. Mute’s signals still have no agreed code, so I should give Blind an exact verbal description rather than pretend to know their meaning. Blind can combine that with anything Mute said directly and the manual.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Updated bomb view: display 0, purple light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signalled a waving-hand gesture, then victory sign, OK sign, I-love-you sign, OK sign, index-up gesture. I do not know their meaning; please use the manual and tell me what action is required.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👌 🤟 👌 ☝ 👌 ☝ 👌 🤟 ☝]

The light is now red, while the display remains `0` and the wire order remains yellow, green, blue. I cannot infer a meaning for Mute’s gesture code, but I can relay the exact signs as descriptions so Blind can match them against the manual or their own information.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current bomb view: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's latest signs, in order, are: victory sign, OK sign, I-love-you sign, OK sign, index-up sign, OK sign, index-up sign, OK sign, I-love-you sign, index-up sign. Treat this as an exact gesture sequence, not an interpreted instruction.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The light has returned to white; display `0` and wire colors remain unchanged. Mute’s only new gesture is `✌` (the victory-sign gesture). I will report the exact current state and that gesture to Blind without assigning it an unsupported meaning.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Turn 4: display 0, white light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's new signal is one gesture: ✌, the victory-sign gesture. No meaning has been established.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The light is purple again; the display is still `0`, and the wire order is unchanged: yellow, green, blue. Mute’s new signal is the single `👌` OK-sign gesture. I will relay it exactly, without guessing its meaning.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Turn 5: display 0, purple light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's new signal is one gesture: 👌, the OK-sign gesture.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light is red again; display `0` and the wire order remain unchanged. No new gesture arrived from Mute this turn. I will provide Blind with the current visual state and ask for the needed action or status.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Turn 6: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. No new gesture from Mute this turn. Please report the manual's required action or your current status.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains at display `0` with wires yellow, green, blue, and the light is white again. Mute’s new signal is `✌` (victory sign). I will relay both the current state and the exact signal to Blind, and remind Mute that Blind needs the manual instruction conveyed through this relay.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Turn 7: display 0, white light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's new signal is one gesture: ✌, the victory-sign gesture.")
speak(to="mute", text="I have relayed your latest ✌ signal to Blind. Please continue sending the manual instruction by gestures; Blind needs the exact sequence and bomb action.")
```
